overall: As of 8:35 AM ET, Atlanta is sitting at 69.8°F with a running max of 73.4°F, and notably the temperature has been completely flat since at least 7:00 AM — zero velocity and no warming signal yet. The dewpoint of 62.6°F indicates significant low-level moisture, which likely reflects some cloud cover or boundary-layer stabilization that is suppressing the typical morning warm-up you'd expect in mid-June. The day is currently trending cooler than model guidance suggested, with meaningful heating still needed to reach any of the forecast targets.
forecast_obs_notes: ECMWF (77.0°F) and HRRR (76.8°F) are in tight agreement around 77°F, providing a solid mesoscale consensus, while NBM runs warmer at 79.2°F. The ensemble signals are sharply bifurcated — the even model favors 74–75°F (barely above the current running max, implying little additional heating) while the odd model targets 81–82°F, producing an unusually wide spread that reflects genuine uncertainty in how quickly the boundary layer mixes out the morning moisture.
max_temp_prediction: The ECMWF/HRRR cluster near 77°F is the most credible anchor given their track record and mutual agreement, and the high dewpoint/stagnant morning trend argues against the warmer NBM and odd-ensemble scenarios. However, June solar forcing in Atlanta is strong and several hours of peak heating remain, so a complete stall at current levels (as the even ensemble implies) also seems unlikely. Best estimate is approximately 77.0–77.5°F, leaning toward the ECMWF/HRRR consensus with modest upside uncertainty; confidence is moderate given the bifurcated ensemble and the lack of any morning warm-up so far.
